CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

a. The Government;
b. Provincial Government
c. Other Regencies/Cities; and
d. Non-governmental institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses in accordance with applicable law.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be set forth in the form of a Joint Agreement.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Government Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Government Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, communities, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Government Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Government Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, communities, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Government Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Government Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, communities, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

5.6.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Government Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Government Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, communities, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

Article 19

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through: a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;

b. education and training for women victims of violence; c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and

d. fostering and enhancing economic independence of women victims of violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be set forth in the form of an Agreement.

Article 18

(1) In order to achieve the objectives of protecting women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 4, the Regional Government may cooperate with:

a. The Government;
b. Provincial Government
c. Other Regencies/Cities; and
d. Non-governmental institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses in accordance with applicable law.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be set forth in the form of a Joint Agreement.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Government Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Government Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, communities, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Government Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Government Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, communities, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Government Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Government Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, communities, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, has sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of being insulted, ashamed, uncomfortable, and unsafe for others. 21. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

Article 25

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Seluma Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various statutory regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the Government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not yet been able to 17 provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer and at the same time provide legal certainty in protecting women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from preventing the occurrence of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation from the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from beloved Seluma Regency.

Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of physical and/or mental violence, child victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of violence to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering physically, psychologically, sexually or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is an act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or occurrence of violence against the victim. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, educators, social institutions, law enforcement officials, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
